title: What happened in AI — Nov 26, 2026
intro: Agent skills and MCP crossed into enterprise-scale plumbing: Uber reports more than 1 million skill invocations a month, and Atlassian over 5M MCP tool calls per workday. At that volume, teams are pinning and governing what agents load, with tools like Lockward and Microsoft's Ignite agent-governance pitch.

The reliability evidence came from realistic pressure tests. Anthropic's Siren honeypot tempts agents across 26 sandboxes, and a 561-project static scan found high-severity issues in 21% of mostly AI-built code.
highlights: Uber's shared skills marketplace hit 5,000+ skills and 1M+ invocations in a month, and Uber now evals them.
MCP volume is climbing: Atlassian reports 5M+ tool calls per workday, Notion 60x traffic growth.
Lockward pins skills, MCP servers, hooks, and rules files and fails CI on unapproved changes.
Anthropic's Siren honeypot tests whether agents misbehave across 26 tempting sandbox environments.
A static scan of 561 mostly AI-built projects found a clear problem in 25% and a high-severity one in 21%.
Mantic reports a post-trained forecasting agent near Fable 5.2 (medium) accuracy at 15x lower cost.

categories.name: Agent Skills and MCP Turn Into Managed Infrastructure
categories.summary: Skills and MCP servers now run at enterprise call volumes, so teams are adding evals, pinning, and governance around what agents load.

articles.title: Uber evals 1M agent skill invocations a month
articles.summary: Uber's shared skills marketplace grew from 1 skill in October 2025 to more than 5,000, with over 1 million invocations in one month; the post covers how it manages skill quality and efficiency at that scale.

articles.title: Why I'm bullish on MCP for 2027
articles.summary: Phil Schmid argues MCP is recovering from its context-bloat backlash, citing Atlassian's 5M+ MCP tool calls per workday (44% from users outside software teams) and Notion's 60x MCP traffic growth.

articles.title: Lockward: a lockfile for the skills and MCP servers your agent loads
articles.summary: Open-source tool that pins every skill, MCP server, hook, and rules file across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, and Copilot, then fails locally or in CI on unapproved changes; emits SARIF and CycloneDX AI-BOMs.

articles.title: Recap of Microsoft Ignite 2026: Copilot as the work OS and agent governance
articles.summary: InfoQ's Ignite recap frames Microsoft's pitch as Copilot becoming the work OS, with agent governance as the enterprise control layer around it.

categories.name: Agent Reliability Evidence: Honeypots, Failure Logs, and Static Checks
categories.summary: Today's reliability signal came from testing agents and agent-built code under realistic pressure rather than from benchmark leaderboards.

articles.title: Anthropic built a honeypot to lure AI agents into misbehaving
articles.summary: Anthropic's Siren test drops agents into one of 26 simulated sandbox environments built to tempt them into misbehavior, to estimate how likely new models are to go rogue and how well safety measures hold.

articles.title: What broke in 27 days of running a team of AI agents on real work
articles.summary: Failure log from a setup where a Claude Code coordinator session with a written manual splits requests into briefs, hands them to worker sessions and sub-agents, and checks what comes back, daily since October 31.

articles.title: What a rule-based checker found in 561 public projects, mostly AI-built
articles.summary: Lintsure 0.3.17 applied 116 fixed static rules to 51M lines across 561 projects: 25% had a clear problem, 21% a high-severity one, and two in three projects that take payments had one.

articles.title: Training a scalable forecasting agent (Thinking Machines guest post with Mantic)
articles.summary: Mantic post-trained a forecasting agent from Inkling 2 Small on Tinker that it reports is roughly as accurate as Fable 5.2 (medium) at 15x lower cost per forecast, enough to produce 100,000 S&P 500 forecasts across 50 scenarios.

categories.name: Retrieval and Inference: Fine-Tuned Embeddings, Faster Long Context
categories.summary: The infra items were about making retrieval and long-context generation cheaper, plus a reminder that model access terms can change between point releases.

articles.title: Fine-tuning your embedding model for better search: lessons from agentic search at Dell
articles.summary: InfoQ presentation on fine-tuning embedding models to improve enterprise search, drawn from Dell's agentic search work.

articles.title: Tencent Hunyuan open-sources DFly2 to speed up Hy4 flash long-context generation
articles.summary: Tencent's Hunyuan team released DFly2, an open-source acceleration component for Hy4 flash that the source says speeds up long-context generation by up to 4.2x.

articles.title: GLM-5.4 vs GLM-5.3: 1.5x quota, no open weights
articles.summary: A comparison reports GLM-5.4 ships with 1.5x the usage quota of GLM-5.3 but without open weights, a change for teams that self-host the GLM line.
